summary: Full-extraction pass over 15 stored Malta documents: the IIP/GCES regulator annual reports 2015-2019 and 2021-2024, the National Development and Social Fund reports for 2020 and 2025, and four consolidated laws (HNWI non-EU rules, Global Residence Programme rules, MRVP and MPRP regulations).

program_terms.quote: The €200 renewal fee for the residency card, at a time when the validity period was 12 months, was seen as an unnecessary charge

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant, first half of the EUR 10,000 deposit, paid at the residency stage (Identity Malta practice)
program_terms.location: PDF p. 40, section 5.1.2; also PDF p. 18 (collection table)
program_terms.quote: IMA has opted to split such payment into two tranches with an initial €5,000 being requested at the very start and the remaining balance being requested once all documentation has been successfully provided.
program_terms.notes: Part of the EUR 650,000 contribution; the regulator notes the split deviates from LN 47 of 2014, which requires EUR 10,000 before the application. The second EUR 5,000 is paid at the full application stage.

events.title: Global Residence Programme rules amended (L.N. 267 of 2014)
events.description: The consolidated rules mark rules 2, 4, 5, 6 and 10 as amended by L.N. 267 of 2014. In the consolidated text: a beneficiary must not be a long-term resident; the EUR 15,000 minimum tax is payable in full both in the year status is granted and in the year it ends, by 30 April with a return proving the conditions; long-term residents are taxed on worldwide income and mandataries who fail to report them face a EUR 10,000 penalty; letting the qualifying property ends the status; a mandatary who fails more than twice loses registration. The exact date of the notice is not printed.
events.location: PDF pp. 1, 4-8, margin notes "Amended by: L.N. 267 of 2014"
events.quote: LEGAL NOTICE 167 of 2013, as amended by Legal Notices 267 of 2014 and 69 of 2020.

events.title: Global Residence Programme: status can pass to a dependant on the beneficiary's death (L.N. 69 of 2020)
events.description: Rule 3 is marked as amended by L.N. 69 of 2020. In the consolidated text, after a beneficiary's death the special tax status is granted to a dependant who inherits the primary residence or rents a qualifying property and meets the other conditions. The consolidation does not show which words of rule 3 the notice changed; the date of the notice is not printed.
events.location: PDF p. 4, rule 3(3), margin note "Amended by: L.N. 69 of 2020"
events.quote: Following the death of a beneficiary, the special tax status granted in terms of sub-rule (2) shall be granted to a dependant of that deceased beneficiary

events.title: MRVP certificates issued after the 2021-22 deadlines declared valid (L.N. 56 of 2024)
events.description: Regulation 11 of the MRVP Regulations, marked as amended by L.N. 56 of 2024, now lets the agency extend any time limit for a valid reason and declares valid for all purposes certificates issued for applications concluded after the deadlines in regulation 5(3A) and (3B) (end-2021 / 31 Mar 2022). The consolidation does not show which words L.N. 56 of 2024 inserted, and the date of the notice is not printed (point-in-time 5 Mar 2024).
events.location: PDF p. 14, reg. 11(3)-(4), margin note "Amended by: L.N. 56 of 2024"
events.quote: Certificates issued by the Malta Residence and Visa Agency in respect of applications which were concluded after the lapse of the time-limits established in sub-regulations (3A) and (3B) of regulation 5, shall be valid for all purposes of the law.

events.title: IIP residence card validity extended from 12 to 18 months
events.description: After agents complained about the EUR 200 renewal fee for a card valid 12 months, Identity Malta extended the validity of the IIP residence card to 18 months (before the report's August 2015 foreword).
events.quote: Identity Malta has already responded by extending the validity period from the original 12 months to 18 months.

events.title: Identity Malta issues revised IIP guidelines
events.description: A more comprehensive set of IIP guidelines setting out the process step by step, including e-residence criteria (health insurance, self-sufficiency, property lease or purchase, Tier 1 due diligence).
events.quote: In May 2015, Identity Malta also released a revised set of Guidelines.

events.title: IIP moved from the Home Affairs ministry
events.description: Responsibility for the IIP was transferred from the Ministry of Home Affairs and National Security (to the Ministry for Justice, Culture and Local Government, per the glossary); reported in January 2016.
events.quote: The two main events of the past 12 months, namely the transfer of the IIP from the Ministry of Home Affairs and National Security and the appointment of a new Regulator

events.title: Malta Residence and Visa Programme launched in practice
events.description: The IIP regulator writes that the residence and visa programme was launched early in May 2016 (the regulations date from August 2015).
events.quote: the Visa and Residence Programme which was launched early in May 2016

events.title: IIP lease agreements must come with a valuation report
events.description: From July 2016 Identity Malta asks for a valuation report with every IIP lease agreement, confirming the rent is at market value (response to the regulator's 2016 recommendation after the "letterbox" article).
events.quote: As of July 2016, a valuation report is requested with all lease agreements submitted, confirming that the rental value is according to the current market value.

events.title: Prime Minister says the IIP will be extended and made more exclusive
events.description: With 1,101 applications received by June 2017 (61% of the cap), the Prime Minister indicated in November 2017, as reported by the media, that the programme would be extended; the MIIPA launched a public consultation reported in January 2018.
events.quote: Such conundrum was resolved in November 2017 when, as reported by the Media, the Prime Minister indicated that the programme would indeed be extended and that it would be more exclusive.

events.title: Court rules for the agency in a refused IIP applicant's case
events.description: First of two 2016 lawsuits by refused IIP applicants (Case 144/2016) decided in favour of the agency after 30 sittings; appeal lodged 13 Jul 2020.
events.quote: judgement, in favour of the Defendant (the Agency), was issued on 25 June 2020.

events.title: Court rules for the agency in second refused IIP applicant's case
events.description: Case 834/2016, brought by a refused IIP applicant, decided in favour of the agency after 24 sittings; an appeal was lodged.
events.quote: judgement in favour of the Defendant (the Agency) was issued on 20th October 2020.

events.title: Court of Appeal confirms ruling for the agency in a refused IIP applicant's case
events.description: Appeal in Case 144/2016 decided on 9 Jun 2022, upholding the 25 Jun 2020 judgment in favour of the agency.
events.quote: judgement by the Court of Appeal was passed 9th June 2022 in full agreement with the Judgement previously pronounced

ledger.contains: Tenth annual report of the Regulator (OR-GCES), 2023 (calendar year), 82 pages. Part 1 (2020 scheme): vetting of 68 applications (53 concluded, 11 refused, 3 withdrawn, 1 closed), agents\u2019 performance, process description (fees, EUR 27.50 card, timelines), FIAU referrals (9), 2 complaints, merit route (out of scope), media, parliamentary questions, Gazette (22 Dec 2023); statistics: 299 eligibility applications (monthly), sex, region counts (Image 1) and shares (Chart 3), citizenships, 616 dependants (type, monthly), eligibility approvals (141, monthly), not approved (23, monthly, region; 14%), citizenship approvals (96, monthly), naturalisations (87 main, 172 dependants, 259 persons; monthly, region, employment, education, age), properties (localities, values, rents), contributions, fees, distributions, suspense, donations (Appendix A per entity, 2022 and 2023), 87 agents. Part 2 (IIP): vetting of 73 applications, process, requests for review, media and parliamentary questions, court case; statistics by year (Tables 8-25: applications, approvals, not approved, naturalisations monthly and per year, dependants, region, employment, education, age, properties by locality and year, values, investments, contributions, distributions, fees, donations with Appendix B per entity). Section 5: combined table (Table 26, sums of recorded figures), vetted applications since 2014 (Table 27), requests for review (Table 28). Existing rows kept (GCES received 299, eligibility 141, rejected 23, contributions EUR 80.55m, inflows EUR 91.16m, NDSF and Consolidated Fund). Rows from earlier years repeated in the IIP tables are recorded only where they are new to this document for 2023 or as totals; year rows identical to the 2022 report\u2019s tables (employment, education, age, locality tables, purchase and lease values) are not repeated. Not recorded because no indicator fits: agents\u2019 performance, FIAU referrals, requests for review, merit-route data. Discrepancies: Appendix A gives 2022 GCES donations as EUR 150,000.00 (2022 report EUR 150,100); Table 26 prints EUR 11,399,00.00 for combined purchase values; text says 1,083,125 vs Appendix 1,083,124.85.

ledger.contains: Eleventh annual report of the Regulator (ORGCEM), calendar 2024, published 2026, 102 pages. Part 1 (2020 scheme): regulator\u2019s vetting, process, complaints, merit route, media (incl. the CJEU case and the Advocate General\u2019s opinion), parliamentary questions, Gazette; statistics: 409 eligibility applications (monthly; per year since 2020; 958 total), sex, region counts (Image 1) and shares, citizenships, 854 dependants (type, monthly), eligibility approvals (164, monthly), not approved (49, monthly, region; 23%), citizenship approvals (183, monthly; per year), naturalisations (173 main, 348 dependants; per year; monthly; region by country of birth; employment; education; age), properties (localities, values, rents), contributions, fees (eligibility and citizenship stages), distributions, suspense, donations (Table 10; Appendix A per entity), 88 agents. Part 2 (IIP): vetting of 6 applications plus 5 re-vetted, requests for review, Gazette (list withdrawn and replaced in Oct 2025), court case; statistics: Tables 12-28 (applications, approvals, not approved per year; naturalisations monthly and per year; dependants; region; employment, education and age for 2024 and averaged 2015-2024; properties 2024 and by locality 2015-2023/2015-2024; values; investments; contributions; distributions; suspense; donations with Appendix B per entity). Section 5: combined table (sums of recorded figures), vetted applications since 2014, requests for review. Existing rows kept (Tables 2, 3 and 16, cumulative IIP figures, 2024 GCES totals, distributions, AG event). Discrepancies: Table 28 donations total EUR 6,128,148.18 vs EUR 6,128,148.13 in text and Appendix B; Table 29 prints administrative fees as "€1,518,5000"; GCES 2022 donations EUR 150,000 here vs EUR 150,100 in the 2022 report.

ledger.contains: Annual report and financial statements of the National Development and Social Fund (NDSF) for 2020, 68 pages. The NDSF is funded entirely by IIP (and later GCES) contributions, so its receipts, holdings and spending are in scope. Contents: governance and founding regulations (LN 161 of 2020 cutting the NDSF share from 70% to 20%, already an event); investment strategy (discretionary, directed and unallocated portfolios), economic and market overview (out of scope), portfolio performance; IIP receipts by year 2016-2020 and since inception; heritage purchase (Preti painting, EUR 1,480,503); social projects earmarked (EUR 109.04m, Table 7) and paid (EUR 0.6m); grants approved Feb 2021; financial highlights and consolidated position; financial statements (net assets, income, changes in net assets, cash flows, notes on contributions paid and commitments). Existing rows kept (receipts 2016-2020, EUR 599,375,449). Added: text total EUR 599.8m, 2019 cumulative, audited 2019 and 2020 receipts, net assets, cash, investments, commitments, grants paid and earmarked. Not recorded because no indicator fits: portfolio returns, investment income and charges, asset allocation, operating expenses (met by a government endowment), staff. Inconsistencies: 2019 receipts EUR 105.9m in the text vs EUR 105,506,520 in the statements; 2019 net assets EUR 570,185,735 (Table 5) vs EUR 570,186,735 (statements).

Annual report and financial statements of the National Development and Social Fund for 2025 (approved 27 Aug 2026), 61 pages (two-column layout). In scope because the NDSF is funded by IIP, 2020-scheme (Community Malta) and Residency Malta contributions: receipts (2025 EUR 50.4m, 2024 EUR 93.6m incl. EUR 0.10m from Residency Malta; EUR 836.5m since inception), portfolio values and investment results (out of scope beyond balances), consolidated position (net assets, cash, investments, commitments), Table 7 targeted funding of 52 social projects and donations (approved and paid, totals EUR 148,772,227 and EUR 50,865,600), cash flows (grants paid, advances to the Housing Authority), notes on each commitment (2024 comparatives; Hope guarantee fund, Mdina illumination, Inspire, MFA youth programme). Existing rows kept (2024 and 2025 receipts, EUR 836,506,572 cumulative, the 2015 founding event). Not recorded because no indicator fits: portfolio returns, asset allocation, investment income, operating expenses (government endowment), ESG and governance text. Inconsistencies: cumulative receipts at end-2024 EUR 786,139,822 (Table 4) vs EUR 786,499,822 (text); 2024 investments EUR 674,212,302 (statements, text) vs EUR 684,212,302 (Table 4); Hospice Malta disbursements EUR 4,797,582 (note 19.6) vs EUR 3,816,019 (Table 7 and later in the note). The previously recorded 2024 and cumulative receipt rows are attributed to mlt-mec/none though they include IIP and Residency Malta money; the new rows use program_id empty where mixed.
